---
title: Local Projects
description: Add local working directories to Lody so desktop, web, and mobile clients can sync project chat history, file diffs, branches, and worktrees.
---

# Local Projects

Lody supports adding any local working directory as a project. We recommend using the desktop app
for this workflow. After a local project is added, Lody keeps it in sync across devices in real
time, including chat history, file-diff views, Git branches, and per-session worktrees.

## Add a Local Project

Lody supports multiple ways to add one:

- In the desktop app, click the add button next to `My Projects`. This opens the local file picker,
  where you can choose a directory to add.
- In non-desktop environments such as servers, use the [CLI project commands](/docs/cli#project-commands),
  for example `npx lody project add [path]`.

## Local-first availability

On the desktop app, projects and sessions already available on the local machine remain usable when
the network is unavailable. You can open them from the local workspace catalog, read their history,
and continue working. Changes made locally are retained and sync when the connection returns.

Cloud-only actions, such as opening a project on another machine or fetching new GitHub data, still
need a network connection. Removing a project from a different device also requires its owning
machine to be online.

## Worktrees on Local Projects

Local projects now use the same worktree workflow as GitHub-linked projects:

- Each session gets its own isolated worktree, created automatically on demand.
- When the session is archived, the worktree is reclaimed automatically.

See [Worktrees](/docs/worktrees) for the full layout and rationale.

## Sync Code Agent History (Codex, Claude Code, and more)

If you have been using Codex or Claude Code directly on a local project, Lody can pull that
existing conversation history in and continue it from any device.

- Open **Settings → Projects**, pick the local project, and trigger a manual sync to import
  history for the agents Lody detects on that machine.
- Once a project is synced, new conversations started in Lody are mirrored back to the
  corresponding CLI (Claude Code, Codex, and other supported ACP-based agents), so both sides
  stay in step.
- Opening an imported conversation refreshes its latest content on demand, so you always see
  what the underlying CLI has.

## Team Visibility for Non-GitHub Projects

Local projects are private by default — only you can see them, even after joining a workspace.

To collaborate on a project that does not live on GitHub:

1. Open **Settings → Projects**.
2. Pick the local project.
3. Toggle team visibility on.

Teammates can then see the project in their sidebar and start sessions against it. As with
[shared machines](/docs/team#team-machine-visibility), only the project owner can change the
visibility setting, and turning it off immediately hides the project from other members.

## Remote Access to Local Projects

From a different device (web, mobile, or another desktop) you can inspect a local project on its
owning machine without having to be in front of it:

- Browse the current Git branch state of the project.
- Start a worktree on the remote machine directly, then continue the work from wherever you are.

This makes phone-driven and laptop-on-the-go workflows work the same way for local projects as
they do for GitHub-linked ones.

## Remove a Project from Another Device

You can remove one of your local projects from desktop or mobile even when the folder belongs to a
different device.

The owning device must be online because Lody sends the delete request to that machine. Before
removing the project, Lody archives its sessions and asks the owning machine to clean up the
project's worktree setup. Removing a project from Lody does not delete the original project folder.

## Current Limitations

- Local projects cannot push to remote branches directly yet, but you can still ask the agent to
  handle the related Git operations for you.
